title: Windfalls recovered through litigation must be returned to the Resilience Fund within 14 days
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.4.4 requires that where a beneficiary receives "financial benefit or reimbursement of any type" from a court, government, investigative body, or regulator that "results in a windfall," those amounts "will be returned by the Beneficiary to the Resilience Fund within 14 days of receipt." A.2.9.1.1.1.4.4.1 enumerates awarded legal costs, damages awarded to the beneficiary, "[m]onies or digital assets located by police or other investigative bodies that were identified as the property of Sky," and interest.

This is subrogation, and it changes the fund's economic character. Support is a recoverable advance: Sky carries the cost while the outcome is uncertain and is made whole when the beneficiary prevails with costs. Over repeated claims, the effective cost of the programme is limited to unsuccessful and uncompensated defenses.

It also removes an incentive problem. Without clawback, a beneficiary who wins costs would be paid twice for the same expense, which would make filing a claim profitable independent of need.

The 14-day clock is tight for an obligation resting entirely on an individual's compliance, and there is no security or escrow behind it — consistent with the rest of the programme, enforcement depends on the ongoing relationship rather than an instrument. The inclusion of recovered Sky property is a different animal: that clause is not subrogation but restitution, ensuring assets identified as Sky's do not become the finder's.
description: Court-awarded costs, damages, interest and recovered Sky property all flow back, which makes Fund support a recoverable advance rather than a grant and prevents double recovery.
